My 1.5 mu is all the land I have, so I plan it carefully. My wife and I both work in town and bring home about 45,000 yuan a year from off-farm jobs, but I keep this field because growing my own grain is cheaper than buying it from the market, and I do not want good farmland to sit idle. I learned how to manage this rotation over 15 years, and I also picked up some book knowledge from high school and from talking to the input dealer and checking prices online. For a plot this small, I calculate every yuan. I cannot afford hired labor, so everything is done by me and my family.

Right now my winter wheat is already in the ground. I sowed it last October 5th with an improved variety, 35 jin of seed per mu. Before sowing I did rotary tillage and put down 80 jin per mu of 18-22-5 compound fertilizer as basal. At green-up in March I topdressed another 80 jin per mu of the same compound. I figure that gives me about 14.4 kg of nitrogen, 17.6 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. The phosphorus is a bit more than the wheat strictly needs, but this 18-22-5 formula is what the dealer stocks, and for 1.5 mu it is not worth my time to buy separate bags of urea and DAP and mix them myself. I have already irrigated twice from my well — once before winter and once at green-up. I will irrigate a third time at grain filling if May turns dry. I will spray insecticide once if I see aphids, but I do not use herbicide on wheat because the rotary tillage and dense crop canopy keep weeds down. I expect about 560 kg per mu this year, same as last year.

After I harvest the wheat around June 5th, I will plant summer maize immediately. I use Xinyu 335 hybrid seed, one package per mu. I will not till the soil again — I sow directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. That saves me 50 yuan and two days of labor, and the summer season is short so I cannot afford to delay sowing. At sowing I will apply 80 jin per mu of 28-6-6 compound fertilizer. That is about 11.2 kg nitrogen, 2.4 kg phosphorus, and 2.4 kg potassium per mu. The 28 percent nitrogen is enough for maize because the growing season is only about four months, and the residual nutrients from the wheat help too. I will irrigate twice — once when the plants are knee-high, and once during grain filling. I will spray herbicide once before the seedlings emerge, and insecticide twice for armyworm and aphids. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

I keep a simple account in my head. Fertilizer for both crops costs me about 320 yuan. Seeds cost about 124 yuan. Pesticides are about 75 yuan and irrigation about 120 yuan. Total cash input is around 640 yuan. If yields are normal I get about 840 kg of wheat and 900 kg of maize. At current prices that is worth about 1,700 yuan. After costs I clear about 1,000 yuan, plus straw for fuel. It is not much money, but it pays for itself and I get clean grain for my family. My neighbors with similar small plots do about the same thing. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest — if I lose yield I would have to buy grain from the market, and that costs more than the extra bag of compound.
